pos.text:
This is more of a neutral review that leans positive. Leaf Blower Revolution is an incremental game with a lot of depth, but the execution is slightly lacking in terms of design and UI. The game starts off really fun, with upgrades and a pretty seamless path forward. However, after you hit Big Leaf Crunch, the game pacing slows to a crawl, with little to do to speed it up other than to just wait. I didn't want to go through this hump, so I stopped after BLCing multiple times. Certain UI aspects also were a little underdeveloped and slightly frustrating.

Also I had issues launching the game. I eventually figured out that it was probably some Steam Cloud save issue. I disabled cloud save on launch and the game was able to launch.

All in all, not a bad game, especially since it is free.

This was fun for a day, but once the BLC/MLC grind kicked in it was...yeah, just read other reviews about it.

For a quick way to kill a day *without* going the full completionist route.

This game is a ruthless time-sink that sucks you in harder than an industrial vacuum! It started quite innocently—raking a few stray leaves off a green lawn, thinking, "Eh, I'll just tidy up a bit and then quit." Two weeks later, I’m sitting in deep space, blasting intergalactic leaves with an atomic blower and offering them up to digital gods. If you’re into the idle/clicker genre and want the wild satisfaction of clearing even the tiniest speck of dust off your screen, buy it without hesitation. Everyone thinks I’m working, but I’m actually just saving the universe from leaves.

Fun but very repetitive.

Leaf Blower Revolution is a simple game, but there's something satisfying about the progression and slowly unlocking new upgrades. It's definitely more of a game you play casually while grinding in the background.

The main downside is that it can get pretty repetitive, but if you enjoy idle and incremental games, there's still a decent amount of fun to be had.

5.2/10 — Not bad, but the repetition really holds it back.

reviews.title: My Favorite Idle Game Ever
reviews.text: Like many others I found this game on steam a while back. At first I was just enjoying the simple concept of just raking and blowing leaves. However it quickly became a favorite with how many various ways to upgrade and prestige. Not to mention the lore. I love when even a game of the most simple concept has an awesome backstory. This game has kept me busy for hours, and I have checked for months to find it on the AppStore. I was overjoyed when this time checking for it wasn’t just a dream. Thank you to the creators for making this game, as well as bringing it to mobile so I can make progress at any time

reviews.title: Help I’m stuck
reviews.text: For some context, I was watching some cookie clicker when the video cut to this game. I thought nothing of it and then it hit me. It was a game, so I decided to download the game. It was really fun, I even got to the celestial plane, and after a month of hiatus, I got back on and decided to to a big leaf crunch, and then when I got far enough, a regular leaf crunch, but when I was expecting the coin shop to appear, there was just nothing. No coin shop, so I couldn’t get the area shop, and now I’m stuck in the first area, with op gear, and I couldn’t even get converters to progress, so I need help.

reviews.title: Addictive
reviews.text: One of the best, most constantly-entertaining idle/incremental games I have ever played. The only thing is that, on a previous account, I got stuck in the stage of progression near the witch. I couldn’t get enough materials for more pyramids floors or to make certain things in the cauldron, I couldn’t get the right modifiers on a certain crafted leaf no matter how hard I tried, etc. other than that, this is pretty much the best game ever made. Keep up the good work, devs! (Also, as a side note, I probably just got stuck because of a skill issue.)

reviews.title: Absolutely Incredible
reviews.text: This game has got to be the best idle game of all time. Hours upon hours worth of content, a ton of lore, and so so so many other things to do. When you think your getting somewhere close to the end, you might as well laugh at yourself, because your not close, trust me. This game has the perfect balance of idling and actual playtime, with the right amount of struggle too. I have been playing this game on PC and was overjoyed to have it come to mobile. Thank you so much for putting this game into my life!

reviews.text: The game itself seems to be very deep, it doesn’t have any annoying ads or popups and it has a nice gameplay loop. However it performs poorly on mobile, it’s hard to click buttons, you get almost no tutorial when you start the game and the buttons are very close to the bottom of the screen causing me to keep closing the game on accident. If the game was cleaned up a bit it could be amazing but these are game breaking issues due to how much you need to use the shops.

It is extremely frustrating to have to do that every 5 min or so. If it is patched out I would be more than happy to change my rating. All in all fantastic game keep up the good work. reviews.title: God’s Greatest Game
reviews.text: I have been playing this game since December 9th, 2020. 12000 hours so far on Steam, and I can say with complete certainty that this is the greatest idle game to ever be released, AND ITS FREE!! I have played quite a few idle games, but there hasn’t been a single one that has kept my interest for this long. There is so much content in this game, and there is always new stuff that is added semi-regularly. It’s nearly impossible to get bored playing this game. This game has grown a massive community on Discord as well, as the main hub for anything LBR related. Cheesetor, the developer (as he’s called on discord), is very passionate about this game and his community. He semi-regularly adds content, he allows us to make suggestions for the game, he listens to criticism, he helps fix bugs, and he’ll even share a beer with you! There are very few game developers who can even come close to how
